atoms.text: This guide configures a bucket to receive network flow records from FlowLens, which writes compressed log files every 10 minutes. Create a bucket named example-flow-logs in the same Region as the monitored network. Attach a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FlowLensDelivery, a role in your own account that the delivery job uses. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flowlens/AWSLogs/444455556666/*. Add a Condition on s3:x-amz-acl requiring bucket-owner-full-control so that the bucket owner can read every delivered object. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN, because the delivery job verifies bucket ownership before the first write. Files appear under the prefix flowlens/AWSLogs/444455556666/ with a date-based key structure. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject or s3:ListBucket to this principal, since the delivery path only needs to create objects.

This guide configures a bucket to receive network flow records from FlowLens, which writes compressed log files every 10 minutes. Create a bucket named example-flow-logs in the same Region as the monitored network. Attach a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the service principal flowlens.amazonaws.com, the identity FlowLens uses when it delivers logs. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flowlens/AWSLogs/444455556666/*. Add Conditions on s3:x-amz-acl requiring bucket-owner-full-control and on aws:SourceAccount equal to 444455556666, so that only FlowLens activity from your account can write. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN, because the delivery job verifies bucket ownership before the first write. Files appear under the prefix flowlens/AWSLogs/444455556666/ with a date-based key structure. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject or s3:ListBucket to this principal, since the delivery path only needs to create objects.

This procedure sets up a bucket for load balancer access logs produced by BalanceGate. BalanceGate flushes a log file for each balancer node roughly every five minutes. Create a bucket named example-lb-logs and enable default encryption with a bucket-managed key. In the bucket policy, add a statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::777788889999:root, the account that operates the balancer fleet and performs the log writes. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-logs/balancegate/*. Do not allow any other action in this statement, because log files are only created and never modified. Enable access logging on each balancer and specify the bucket name and the prefix balancegate. Confirm delivery by checking for a test file named ELBAccessLogTestFile under that prefix within a few minutes.

This procedure sets up a bucket for load balancer access logs produced by BalanceGate. BalanceGate flushes a log file for each balancer node roughly every five minutes. Create a bucket named example-lb-logs and enable default encryption with a bucket-managed key. In the bucket policy, add a statement with Principal set to the service principal logdelivery.balancegate.amazonaws.com, which is the identity BalanceGate presents when it writes logs. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-logs/balancegate/*, and add an aws:SourceArn condition matching your balancer ARNs. Do not allow any other action in this statement, because log files are only created and never modified. Enable access logging on each balancer and specify the bucket name and the prefix balancegate. Confirm delivery by checking for a test file named ELBAccessLogTestFile under that prefix within a few minutes.

This guide describes the bucket configuration required to store API audit events recorded by TrailKeeper. TrailKeeper writes one gzip-compressed JSON file per Region roughly every five minutes. Create a bucket named example-audit-trail with versioning enabled and block all public access. Add a policy statement with Principal set to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/TrailKeeperWriter and Action s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN, so the writer can confirm the bucket owner. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/trailkeeper/AWSLogs/222233334444/*. Include a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control on the write statement. Objects are placed under a path of the form trailkeeper/AWSLogs/222233334444/Region/year/month/day. Retention should be handled by a lifecycle rule on the prefix, not by granting delete permissions to the writer.

This guide describes the bucket configuration required to store API audit events recorded by TrailKeeper. TrailKeeper writes one gzip-compressed JSON file per Region roughly every five minutes. Create a bucket named example-audit-trail with versioning enabled and block all public access. Add a policy statement with Principal set to the service principal trailkeeper.amazonaws.com and Action s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN, so the service can confirm the bucket owner. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/trailkeeper/AWSLogs/222233334444/*. Include Conditions requiring s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control and aws:SourceArn to match your trail ARN on the write statement. Objects are placed under a path of the form trailkeeper/AWSLogs/222233334444/Region/year/month/day. Retention should be handled by a lifecycle rule on the prefix, not by granting delete permissions to the writer.

This section explains how to receive content delivery request logs from EdgeRelay in a bucket. EdgeRelay batches viewer request records and uploads them as files every few minutes. Create a bucket named example-edge-logs and place it in a Region that EdgeRelay supports for log storage. Write a bucket policy statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::555566667777:user/edgerelay-log-writer, an IAM user in your account whose credentials are configured in the log delivery job. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/* and require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control. Add a separate statement with the same Principal allowing s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket itself. Set the log prefix in the distribution settings to edge/ so that every file falls within the permitted resource path. Verify by requesting a test page through the distribution and finding a new object under edge/ after about ten minutes.

This section explains how to receive content delivery request logs from EdgeRelay in a bucket. EdgeRelay batches viewer request records and uploads them as files every few minutes. Create a bucket named example-edge-logs and place it in a Region that EdgeRelay supports for log storage. Write a bucket policy statement with Principal set to the service principal delivery.edgerelay.amazonaws.com, the identity used by the EdgeRelay log pipeline. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/*, require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control, and add an aws:SourceAccount condition for 555566667777. Add a separate statement with the same Principal allowing s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket itself. Set the log prefix in the distribution settings to edge/ so that every file falls within the permitted resource path. Verify by requesting a test page through the distribution and finding a new object under edge/ after about ten minutes.

This guide covers storing object-level access logs generated by AccessScribe for a source bucket. AccessScribe records each request made against the monitored bucket and groups records into log files. Create a separate target bucket named example-access-log-target; never use the monitored bucket as its own target. In the target bucket policy, add a statement with Principal set to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/AccessScribeDeliveryRole. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-access-log-target/scribe-logs/*. Add a Condition using ArnLike on aws:SourceArn is not available for this principal type, so scope the Resource path to the prefix and restrict writes with s3:x-amz-acl set to bucket-owner-full-control. Enable logging on the monitored bucket and set the target prefix to scribe-logs/. Log files typically show up within a few hours and are named with a timestamp and a random suffix. Apply a lifecycle rule that expires the objects after 90 days.

This guide covers storing object-level access logs generated by AccessScribe for a source bucket. AccessScribe records each request made against the monitored bucket and groups records into log files. Create a separate target bucket named example-access-log-target; never use the monitored bucket as its own target. In the target bucket policy, add a statement with Principal set to the service principal logging.accessscribe.amazonaws.com. Set Action to s3:PutObject and Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-access-log-target/scribe-logs/*. Add Conditions using ArnLike on aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:s3:::example-monitored-bucket and StringEquals on aws:SourceAccount set to 888899990000, which limits writes to that one source. Enable logging on the monitored bucket and set the target prefix to scribe-logs/. Log files typically show up within a few hours and are named with a timestamp and a random suffix. Apply a lifecycle rule that expires the objects after 90 days.

This section describes a bucket that stores DNS query logs from NameWatch for a hosted zone. NameWatch emits query records in batches and writes them as compressed files. Create a bucket named example-dns-query-logs in the Region required by the zone's log configuration. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::123456123456:role/NameWatchLogRole, the role that the query logging configuration assumes within your account. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/namewatch/zone-logs/* and s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN. Require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control on the write action. Specify the bucket ARN and the namewatch/zone-logs/ prefix when you enable query logging for the zone. Expect new objects to appear within about 15 minutes of the first query, with keys that include the zone ID and a timestamp.

This section describes a bucket that stores DNS query logs from NameWatch for a hosted zone. NameWatch emits query records in batches and writes them as compressed files. Create a bucket named example-dns-query-logs in the Region required by the zone's log configuration. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the service principal delivery.namewatch.amazonaws.com, the identity NameWatch uses for query log delivery. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/namewatch/zone-logs/* and s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN. Require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control on the write action, and add aws:SourceAccount set to 123456123456. Specify the bucket ARN and the namewatch/zone-logs/ prefix when you enable query logging for the zone. Expect new objects to appear within about 15 minutes of the first query, with keys that include the zone ID and a timestamp.

This guide prepares a bucket to hold web firewall request logs from ShieldWatch. ShieldWatch buffers sampled and blocked request records and uploads them as JSON files at 5-minute intervals. Name the bucket with the required prefix, for example shieldwatch-logs-example-bucket, because the log destination validation checks the name. Create a bucket policy statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::999900001111:role/ShieldWatchFirehoseRole, the role in your account that performs the upload. Set Action to s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectAcl, with Resource arn:aws:s3:::shieldwatch-logs-example-bucket/AWSLogs/999900001111/ShieldWatch/*. Add a second statement for the same Principal with s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN. Enable logging on the web ACL and select this bucket as the destination. Check that files appear under AWSLogs/999900001111/ShieldWatch/ with hourly path segments after traffic reaches the protected resource.

This guide prepares a bucket to hold web firewall request logs from ShieldWatch. ShieldWatch buffers sampled and blocked request records and uploads them as JSON files at 5-minute intervals. Name the bucket with the required prefix, for example shieldwatch-logs-example-bucket, because the log destination validation checks the name. Create a bucket policy statement with Principal set to the service principal delivery.shieldwatch.amazonaws.com, which ShieldWatch uses when it uploads. Set Action to s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectAcl, with Resource arn:aws:s3:::shieldwatch-logs-example-bucket/AWSLogs/999900001111/ShieldWatch/*, and add aws:SourceAccount set to 999900001111. Add a second statement for the same Principal with s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN. Enable logging on the web ACL and select this bucket as the destination. Check that files appear under AWSLogs/999900001111/ShieldWatch/ with hourly path segments after traffic reaches the protected resource.

This procedure configures a bucket to receive resource configuration history files from ConfigLedger. ConfigLedger delivers a snapshot file every 6 hours and a change history file whenever a recorded resource changes. Create a bucket named example-config-history and enable versioning so that overwritten snapshots are retained. Add a policy statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::333344445555:role/ConfigLedgerRecorder, the recorder role in the account being tracked. Allow s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN so the recorder can validate the destination. Add a second statement with the same Principal allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-config-history/ledger/AWSLogs/333344445555/ConfigLedger/*, with s3:x-amz-acl set to bucket-owner-full-control. Choose the bucket and the key prefix ledger when you create the delivery channel. Verify the setup by requesting a manual snapshot and locating the resulting file under the account-specific path.

This procedure configures a bucket to receive resource configuration history files from ConfigLedger. ConfigLedger delivers a snapshot file every 6 hours and a change history file whenever a recorded resource changes. Create a bucket named example-config-history and enable versioning so that overwritten snapshots are retained. Add a policy statement with Principal set to the service principal configledger.amazonaws.com and a condition of aws:SourceAccount equal to 333344445555. Allow s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN so the service can validate the destination. Add a second statement with the same Principal allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-config-history/ledger/AWSLogs/333344445555/ConfigLedger/*, with s3:x-amz-acl set to bucket-owner-full-control. Choose the bucket and the key prefix ledger when you create the delivery channel. Verify the setup by requesting a manual snapshot and locating the resulting file under the account-specific path.
